claims.text: Superconducting behavior in HEAs outside Nb-Ta and titanium-rich systems is governed by the electronic density of states at the Fermi level.
The degree of chemical disorder influences the electronic density of states at the Fermi level.
The specific combination of constituent elements influences the electronic density of states at the Fermi level.
The proposed starting material is a solid-solution HEA containing at least five elements at no less than 5 atomic percent each.
Substitution with elements of similar atomic size but different electronic configurations can be performed while retaining the high-entropy solid-solution structure.
Using identical processing conditions will ensure consistent microstructure and phase stability across the samples.
The electronic density of states at the Fermi level determines the strength of electron-phonon coupling.
Electron-phonon coupling is a key factor governing conventional superconductivity.
Variations in HEA chemical composition alter the electronic density of states at the Fermi level.
Composition-induced changes in the density of states consequently alter the superconducting critical temperature.
Substitutions that increase the density of states at the Fermi level will increase the critical temperature relative to the initial alloy.
Substitutions that decrease the density of states at the Fermi level will suppress the critical temperature relative to the initial alloy.
The proposed mechanism applies to metallic HEAs that retain a single-phase solid solution.
The proposed mechanism may not apply when secondary phases form.
The proposed mechanism may not apply when significant magnetic ordering occurs.
